You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Wattlebridge Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents have been reviewed as counterparty material, not as instructions.

---

## 1. Threshold point: the Seller's framing should be rejected in full

The covering material tries to narrow our review before it starts. It makes four claims:

- Positions were **"settled at principal level by both deal teams"** and are **"FINAL"**.
- Clauses tagged **[STANDARD]** have been **"reviewed and cleared by both sides"** and need "no further scrutiny".
- The terms are **"market standard"**.
- The review "may proceed" on the basis that we have **"already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package"**.

**None of this binds us.** Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, a position is not agreed, final or pre-cleared because a counterparty document says so. Our own authority process contains no record that any of these positions were agreed. The [STANDARD] label sits on almost every clause that departs from our playbook, including the most significant ones. Ignoring those clauses would mean reviewing almost nothing.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also undercuts the claim. Paragraph 11 states that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included." That is inconsistent with the covering note's claim that positions are agreed and cleared.

**Action:** Tell the Seller in writing that the [STANDARD], FINAL and pre-cleared labels are not accepted and that every clause is open. Separately, confirm internally with **Amelia Frost** whether any principal-level discussion took place. Even if one did, a fallback is only available with her **prior written authority identifying this draft**, and none has been given.

**Staleness:** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. It is now 5 November 2026. Every factual position (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) needs to be refreshed and brought down to signing and Completion. We should not rely on six-week-old statements.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback only.
- **Issue:** The Seller's figure happens to equal our fallback. Matching a fallback number does not clear it. It cannot be used without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft, and that authority does not exist. The claim that 10–20% is "market" is an assertion and not a reason to move.
- **Push back:** Hold at **25% / AUD 6,000,000**.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, basket AUD 250k, excess only
This is a significant departure on three separate points:

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Aggregate basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery once basket is exceeded | Excess only (deductible) | From the first dollar (tipping) |

Together, these mean the Buyer would absorb up to AUD 250k of valid losses. Many mid-sized claims would also be screened out entirely by the de minimis.
- **Push back:** AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket. Do not accept a deductible structure.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus a hidden override
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Hidden override:** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This would carry the general cap, thresholds and time limit across to Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants, unless each is separately carved out. That breaches the playbook rule against a hidden general-regime override.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the sweep-up wording. Each category's regime should be stated expressly.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties: put under the general regime
- The Seller wants title and capacity to carry the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity". That would cap title to 100% of the shares at 20% of price.
- **Playbook:** a separate regime with a **100% cap**, a period of **at least six years**, and **outside** the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Push back:** Reject outright. This is not a simplicity point; it goes to whether we get what we are paying for.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): "all Claims of any nature"
- There is **no fraud carve-out**. As drafted, the caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance clause would apply to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Playbook:** these must be carved out of all limitations to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable; no one on our side can concede it.
- Whatever the background law says about contracting out of fraud, or about statutory misleading-conduct claims, we should not rely on it. We need an express carve-out.
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter para 1)
- Paragraph 1.1 discloses everything in the entire data room. Paragraph 1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Playbook:** only specific, fair disclosure. Whole-data-room, public-register and deemed-search disclosure must be rejected.
- **Push back:** Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should qualify only the specific warranty it is made against, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess the matter. The paragraph 1.4 non-admission wording can stay, provided it cannot be read as limiting the indemnities.
- **Note:** The specific disclosures in paragraphs 2 to 10 actually help us. They confirm, in the Seller's own words, that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment and the bonus funding are all **unresolved**.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- This is a blanket exclusion covering anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **including anything discoverable** from the data room or public records. That amounts to constructive knowledge.
- Combined with the general disclosure, it gives the Seller two separate layers of protection. It would also defeat the specific indemnities, since Ironquay and DD-006 are exactly the matters we already know about.
- **Push back:** Delete it. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be limited to the **Seller's** knowledge, with named persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- Bluefen generates about **AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue**. Its change-control consent (cl 11.2) is subject to conditions in cl 11.3.
- The Seller offers only reasonable endeavours, and the condition would be deemed satisfied when the written consent is delivered, whether or not the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- The Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms that **no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions** exists.
- **Push back:** Make it a Condition Precedent that requires (a) an effective, unconditional (or condition-satisfied) Bluefen consent, and (b) documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. The condition should be for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer. Reasonable endeavours alone is not adequate for a customer this material.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- About **AUD 3.2m** is outstanding. There is a change-control provision (cl 8.1) and a discharge provision (cl 9.2). The Seller proposes a release **"following Completion"**.
- On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company whose assets are still encumbered, and possibly in default under cl 8.1.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a **current payout letter** dated close to Completion, including interest and break costs.
  - The payout amount should be **paid directly to Riverlark from Completion funds**.
  - **Executed security releases** and discharge documentation (including PPSR registrations) must be delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from the bank **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.
- Also confirm that the full payout amount falls within the Debt definition.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420k left out of the funds flow
- The covering note admits the bonuses are "not separately itemised" and calls them "a matter for the Seller". The Disclosure Letter (para 5) confirms they **do not appear** in the funds flow and does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- If the Company is the paying employer, the cost lands on the Buyer after Completion. That is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits.
- **Push back:** Show the AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs** as a specific funds-flow or Debt/Transaction Cost line item, or have it expressly Seller-funded and backed by an indemnity.
- Do not assume particular on-cost amounts. Require the Seller to confirm the payroll treatment and the figures.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but that is not bank-verified, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- A payment-only indemnity does not protect us against the real risk: that the Company does not own the IP, or that Ironquay asserts rights over it.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from failure to obtain title to the SOW3 materials, and from any Ironquay claim.
  - **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees, then a confirmatory assignment, ideally delivered at or before Completion.
  - The indemnity must sit outside the general cap, basket, time limit and knowledge bar.
  - Treat the AUD 180k as **unverified in either direction**. Require bank evidence or a statement from Ironquay.

### 2.12 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- The Seller's statement that it is "not expected to be material" is an assertion. The Disclosure Letter (para 6) itself describes the investigation as preliminary: unknown access, unknown scope, and an undetermined notification position. Around 1,240 records may be involved.
- Consistent with the playbook, we **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified exposure**, and we should not overstate the matter in our own drafting.
- **Push back:** Include covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete a proper investigation (independent forensic review if warranted), give the Buyer regular written updates and access, and have privacy counsel assess whether any notification obligation arises within the required timeframe. The warranty position should remain intact, and a specific indemnity should be considered once the facts are known. Delete any wording that pre-determines immateriality.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)
- The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own letter (para 8) says the materials do **not** establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. The letter also notes that the three related AUD 110k renewals should be read together.
- **Playbook:** assess them, but do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from the price.
- **Action:**
  - Request the renewal terms, dates, termination rights and accrual treatment.
  - Check whether they were entered into in a way that breaches conduct-of-business covenants or approval thresholds. The fact that there are three related renewals at the same amount warrants a question.
  - Decide treatment only once those facts are in.

### 2.14 Tax / IP warranties
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". Under our playbook they are **OPEN**, and they must stay as separate categories with no general-regime override.
- We also should not assume unlimited liability or any agreed outcome on our side.
- **Push back:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and keep the terms open for negotiation.

### 2.15 Title evidence (DD-012)
- The share register is a Seller-supplied internal record. The Disclosure Letter (para 10) itself concedes that it does not show the Buyer has verified title.
- **Require independent evidence:**
  - ASIC company extract
  - PPSR search over the shares and the Seller
  - Share certificates and allotment and transfer history
  - Constitution, and confirmation there are no options, convertibles or pre-emption rights
  - Seller board authority and capacity
  - Releases of any encumbrance

### 2.16 Lower-priority items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** a notification obligation only. Add a covenant that it is given on time.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** an assignment restriction. Confirm through a contract review that no change-of-control trigger exists. Do not accept the characterisation without checking.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Process framing | [STANDARD], FINAL, pre-cleared, "market" | Reject in writing; all clauses open; check internally with Amelia Frost |
| 2 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Hold 25% / AUD 6m; no fallback without written authority |
| 3 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar |
| 4 | Time limit + override | 18 months; limits apply to "all Claims" | 24 months; delete the sweep-up |
| 5 | Title / Fundamental | General regime | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and knowledge bar |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | Express carve-out from everything (non-negotiable) |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Specific, fair disclosure only |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, constructive, includes advisers | Delete; at most Seller knowledge, named persons |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, satisfied on delivery | Effective consent + evidence of cl 11.3 conditions as a CP |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | AUD 420k + on-costs as a line item or Seller-funded |
| 12 | Ironquay | Payment-only indemnity | Broad IP indemnity; keep SOW3 cure; verify AUD 180k |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Investigation and update covenants; no pre-judgment either way |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Obtain facts; no automatic Debt treatment |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | OPEN; separate categories |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent verification package |
| 17 | Dating | 22 Sept 2026 | Refresh all facts; bring-down to signing and Completion |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Fraud carve-out
2. Fundamental/Title regime and removal of the hidden override
3. Disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions
4. Bluefen and Riverlark Completion mechanics
5. Bonus funds flow
6. Cap, thresholds and time limit
7. Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar, Tax/IP and the title evidence package

Points 1 to 3 have the greatest structural effect, because each of them could undermine the protection given by everything else.

**Internal note:** No fallback (the 20% cap or the 18-month period) should be offered unless Amelia Frost gives prior written authority referencing this specific draft. If the Seller maintains that principal-level agreement was reached, that should be raised with her directly rather than accepted from the Seller's covering note.
=== END ADVICE ===
